claims.claim: Severian was Bishop of Gabala in Syria.
Severian flourished from around 400 until 404 as a popular preacher in Constantinople.
Severian was born in the 4th century and died after 408.
Severian spoke Greek with a pronounced Syrian accent.
De caeco et Zacchaeo was formerly attributed to John Chrysostom as author.
The authenticity of De caeco et Zacchaeo as a work of Severian was confirmed by Sever J. Voicu in 1983-1984.
De caeco et Zacchaeo survives in two recensions, a shorter and a longer one.
The work is preserved in Patrologia Graeca 59, columns 599-610.
De caeco et Zacchaeo has been transmitted among the spuria attributed to John Chrysostom.
The work is catalogued as CPG 4592 in the Clavis Patrum Graecorum.
The incipit of De caeco et Zacchaeo is Πολλαὶ καὶ διάφοροι τῶν ἁγίων Γραφῶν.
The work is listed in the Bibliotheca Hagiographica Graeca as BHG 2475e.
SCOPE: this English is De caeco et Zacchaeo, stored for severianus-de-caeco-zacchaeo. De caeco nato is a different sermon.
